title: Hold on the Synth tab, patterns, and mouth wubs
thisBuild: The Synth tab has Hold's full settings over its keys: the count, − and +, and Let go. Set it to 3, hold a chord, then play single notes on top, like on the Padiano. (Your note: with only the dock's H there, a count of Last or 8 made every note take the hold.)
🎹 On pads, next to the pad number on the Synth tab, opens that synth's Padiano on the pad grid. Its ◎ button takes you back to the knobs.
Padiano sizes now go S, M, L and XL (⚙ on the Padiano). XL is much taller, with wider squares. Rows 1, 2 or 3: each row up is the same notes an octave higher.
Repeat patterns: tap the rate under RPT on the dock. PATTERN has ready ones (2 on 1 off, On off, Gallop, Tresillo, Clave) and a strip you tap to make your own. Held notes follow the pattern too.

Mouth control (☰ menu, or add MTH to the dock with ⋯): tap Listen and make sounds. Ooo closes the picked pad's filter, eee opens it, so "wow wow wow" over a held synth is a wub. Pick what the vowel and your loudness move. With Rec on while the loop plays, it records like a finger on XY.
watch: On the Synth tab: Hold on, count 3, play three notes, then play more. The first three should keep going and the rest play only while you hold them.
Mouth control with headphones, then on the speaker. Send a note on how fast it follows you and whether the music moves it on its own.
Try a pattern with Hold and a synth, while stopped and while playing.
limits: Mouth control hears the music through the speaker. Headphones work best; turn Sensitivity down if it moves while you're quiet.
It follows the vowel and the loudness, not your pitch. Camera mouth tracking isn't built yet.
A Mono synth still plays one note at a time, held or not.
